newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF FRENCH AND SWEDISH DAVIS CUP TEAMS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF FRENCH AND SWEDISH DAVIS CUP TEAMS.

text.p: Profiles of Swedish and French teams for the Davis Cup final starting on Friday:

STEFAN EDBERG, age 30 height 1.88 m, weight 77 kg. Married with a daughter. Took up tennis aged seven. Turned professional 1983 when he was world number one junior and first player to win junior grand slam of French, Wimbleon, U.S. and Australian titles. Has won 41 singles titles including six grand slams -- Australian, Wimbledon and U.S Opens twice. He has helped Sweden to lift Davis Cup four times. A serve and volley player with a fine temperament and looked on as the gentleman of the tennis circuit, Edberg was world number one at end of 1990 and 1991. Carried Sweden's flag at Barcelona Olympics in 1992 and will retire after the Davis Cup.

THOMAS ENQVIST, 22, 1.91 m, 85 kg. Started playing at age five. Captured 1991 Australian Open and Wimbledon Junior titles, finishing year at number one junior. He is coached by Joakim Nystrom and has won seven singles titles in his career two of them in the last few weeks at Paris and Stockholm. Has come on in leaps and bounds over past year and is highest ranked player in final at number nine. In 1994 he underwent two knee operations, but ended 1995 as number one ranked Swede and is seen as Edberg's natural successor. NICKLAS KULTI, 25, 1.90 m, 78 kg. Won 11 national junior titles. Finished 1989 as number one ranked junior player in world. Won 1989 Wimbledon and Australian Open junior before turning professional in 1989. Has two singles and three doubles title to his name. In 1995 he had foot surgery on Sept 20 and missed rest of year. Reached French Open doubles final in 1995 with Magnus Larsson.

JONAS BJORKMAN, 24, 1.84m, 76 kg. Won Swedish Junior Championship at 18 after starting playing at six years old. Has 10 doubles titles to his name. In Davis Cup final against Soviet Union in 1994 won five-set doubles with Jan Apell.

CEDRIC PIOLINE, 27, 1.89m, 79 kilos. Married with one son. The son of a former Romanian volleyball international, Pioline has for long been the odd man out in France's tennis circles. Had a serious knee operation at the age of 13 after a fall. Talented and without serious weaknesses, he was coached from 1990 and 1993 by university teacher Henri Dumont, who led him to the U.S. Open final in 1993. But Dumont's controversial methods and his wish that Pioline should not play the Davis Cup led to a clash. Ranked ninth in the world in 1994, Pioline lost nine consecutive finals before winning his first title in Copenhagen this year. Still moody at times, he has become since parting with Dumont

ARNAUD BOESTCH, 27, 1.83, 76kg. Married with one son. France's greatest tennis prospect at the age of 14, Boetsch struggled a few years before asserting himself on the pro circuit. Fitness and a punishing forehand are his main weapons. But Boestch, who can beat anyone on a good day, still has too many ups and downs to remain among the world's top players for long. Won three titles in his career and recently scored a morale boosting win over Swede Thomas Enqvist in Lyon. A member of the winning team of 1991, he lived France's historical victory on the bench as first reserve.

GUY FORGET, 31, 1.90, 80 kg. Married with two sons. The son of a tennis player, Guy Forget had to wait for nine years on the professional circuit to live up to the promise shown as a junior. The 1982 Orange Bowl winner shone more as a doubles player than in singles, his frail figure and withdrawn personality perhaps to blame. Won the first of his 10 singles titles in Toulouse in 1986, emulating his father and grandfather who won the same tournament. Had his best year in 1991, winning six of his 10 career tournaments to reach number four in the world rankings before leading France to win the Davis Cup final by beating Pete Sampras. GUILLAUME RAOUX, 26, 1.80m, 77k. Married with one son. A solid but physically limited singles player, Raoux has had his best results playing doubles. The bespectacled Parisian, who spends most of his time in Florida, won the Orange Bowl doubles title in 1986. Winner of his first singles title in 1992, in Brisbane, he became this year the perfect doubles partner for Forget.
